text:
Years of accumulated shit in your guts (not in the phases, but Phase 4 comes closest): This part isn't in the gut healing books I read, but even if you fix all of what's going into you now, if you're already full and clogged with all of what went in before, that's gonna be little help. My friend Pooyan got incredibly healthier and happier after getting enough colon hydrotherapy to flush that stuff out, combined with then also doing intense stretches like hanging from one arm, until finally, the most crusted up shit exploded in him which was very painful for a day.

This is likely caused by diverticulosis, a disease that causes herniated pockets (called diverticula) to form in the intestines which aren't supported by smooth muscle. There's no known cure for this disease, except possibly glutamine, based on one incomplete clinical trial, which found 2 of 9 women had incredible reductions in diverticula. Glutamine is an amino acid that's the fuel for small intestinal cells, so this makes some sense. 10% of people get side effects from it (including constipation). Butyrate, a fatty acid your gut bacteria make, is the fuel for the colon cells. I would also suggest diosmin, a compound from citrus fruits, for improving blood vessel integrity.

However, while we don't know if Pooyan has diverticulosis, what we now do know is that his peak health disappeared 3 days later after eating some bread with A1 dairy, the regular cow's milk that has the A1 type of casein protein.

CAUTION: If you have severe diverticulosis, especially diverticulitis (once the fecal impaction causes intestinal infection & inflammation), you might be at high risk for intestinal wall rupture, and even rejected by the more reputable colonic irrigation clinics. Make sure you get cleared first by a gastroenterologist, a doctor who specializes in the gut.

Poor diet now (Phase 2): industrial and processed foods, especially oils, are often empty calories full of countless toxins and oxidation byproducts. Toxins are sequestered in fat cells to prevent them from damaging organs, but this toxic fat (especially the visceral fat around your organs) becomes a chronic health issue even as it protects us from immediately dying from the sequestered toxins.

Parasites, the stomach bacteria H. pylori, mold, metals (Phases 3 and 6): We are often addicted to junk food due to a vicious cycle in which the junk feeds parasitic organisms and bad bacteria, yeast, etc, which then send signals to our brain to consume more junk. Thus, we have to target the problem from various angles--cleansing out pathogens, repopulating good bacteria, addressing vitamin (especially thiamine), mineral, and enzyme deficiencies, and changing what we eat. I wrote about my detox protocol (which includes the gut) here. For H. pylori specifically: if you get heartburn when your stomach is empty only, that's usually H. pylori, and it's easily treated with berberine, an extract from plants like barberry.

placement: The causes list, impaction to parasites, in his order; each note inside the sentence that first uses the term.

questions.Q1: PASS: each term note comes right where the term first appears, or in the next sentence, and the sentence's own point still comes first; the caution's instruction now follows its warning
questions.Q2: PASS: every instruction says what it is for in the reader's terms (take it away from meals so food doesn't compete; check with your oncologist before the 5g)
questions.Q3: PASS: each term note names the exact thing (the A1 type of casein protein; the seals between the cells of your gut lining; the first milk a cow makes after giving birth)
questions.Q4: PASS: each new "it", "that" and "this" has its object in the sentence before
questions.Q5: PASS: each "so", "but" and "because" has the claim it turns on said before it
questions.Q6: PASS: the notes sit where a reader first needs them; nothing moved except the caution's instruction, up to where a reader with cancer needs it
questions.Q7: PASS: each note helps this reader act on the sentence it explains

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first; a study after the question it answers)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
